name: Count It: Closest Without Going Over
why_it_works: Counting is a puzzle anyone can try in a few seconds, and an estimate feels like skill rather than luck. The 'without going over' rule makes people slow down and actually look at the work, so they notice how much went into it, and the held-back answer brings them back for the follow-up post.

hook.pattern: Show one finished piece and dare the viewer to estimate how many small parts went into it.
examples: Count fast. Closest without going over wins.

variables.name: item
variables.description: The single finished piece being counted, 3 words or fewer

variables.name: count_unit
variables.description: The small parts people count, plural, 4 words or fewer

variables.name: clue
variables.description: One honest clue, a short sentence starting with a capital, 7 words or fewer
variables.example: More than the candles on a 50th

variables.name: anchor_number
variables.description: A reference number to guess over or under

variables.name: prize
variables.description: What the closest guess wins, with its value in the official rules, 4 words or fewer

variables.name: deadline
variables.description: When guesses close and the real count drops, 4 words or fewer

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 hero photo of the {{item}} from {{brand}} on a plain pedestal, every {{count_unit}} visible, even soft light, clean background
Macro detail of the {{item}} showing a dense patch of {{count_unit}}, raking side light, shallow depth of field, vertical 9:16

beats.purpose: slow turn so they can count
beats.voiceover: Count fast, then comment one number.

visual.prompt: Slow 360 turntable rotation of the {{item}} on the pedestal, every side of the {{count_unit}} shown once, soft even light, vertical 9:16

cta: Comment one number by {{deadline}}. Closest without going over wins {{prize}}. Official rules: {{rules_link}}.

slides.headline: How many {{count_unit}}?
slides.visual_prompt: Hero photo of the {{item}} on a plain pedestal, every part visible, soft even light, 4:5

slides.headline: Clue one
slides.visual_prompt: Macro detail of a dense patch of {{count_unit}} on the {{item}}, raking side light

slides.headline: Over or under {{anchor_number}}?
slides.body: Lock one number in the comments before you swipe.
slides.visual_prompt: Bold type card in {{brand}} colors with the anchor number huge and a question mark

slides.headline: The estimator's trick
slides.body: Count one small patch, count how many patches, then multiply. It beats guessing every time.
slides.visual_prompt: The {{item}} photo with a thin grid drawn over it and one square highlighted

slides.headline: How the winner is picked
slides.body: Closest without going over. A tie goes to a random draw. Official rules: {{rules_link}}.
slides.visual_prompt: Clean rules card in {{brand}} colors with a number line and a stop marker

slides.headline: Real count drops {{deadline}}
slides.body: We post the count and the winner together. No purchase necessary.
slides.visual_prompt: {{brand}} logo card with the prize photo inset and the deadline in large type

craft.notes: The anchor number gives people a reference point so guesses cluster and the comments start comparing. Never show the real count in the ad; post it with the winner in a follow-up, which turns one ad into a two-post series.

do_not: Change the real count after guesses come in
Hide parts of the piece so nobody could estimate fairly
Announce a winner without showing the real count and the comment that won
compliance: Official rules linked: eligibility (age and location), start and end dates, how the winner is picked (closest without going over, ties by random draw) and prize value
No purchase necessary; void where prohibited
Say the contest is not sponsored or run by the platform
Pick the winner by the stated method only, never by likes
